description: Add the public `you worker-sessions list|show|stream|read` command family over authoritative Provider Session and recording projections so operators can correlate Work, state, token usage, duration, events, transcripts, and failures without runtime logs or raw rollout-file inspection.

context.customerAsk: Expose authoritative Provider Session and recording projections through `you worker-sessions list|show|stream|read` so operators can correlate sessions to Work, inspect state, tokens and duration, follow live activity, read a completed transcript, and understand failures from the CLI alone.
context.problem: The current CLI has no cohesive worker-session inspection surface. Operators diagnosing active or failed workers must read runtime logs and provider-specific rollout storage directly, cannot reliably connect an attempt to its Work, and may receive an unexplained FAILED result with no usable cause.
context.solution: Publish narrow query and streaming operations from the services that already own Provider Session inspection and recorded Factory Events, then adapt them into four commands with deterministic human output, stable JSON, typed errors, and explicit streaming termination and cancellation. The CLI consumes canonical projections and never creates a second storage model or parses raw rollout files.

acceptanceCriteria: `you worker-sessions list --work-id <id>` and `you worker-sessions show --provider <provider> --kind <kind> --id <id>` report authoritative Work correlation, lifecycle state, token usage, elapsed duration, and available failure diagnostics for recorded attempts, including multiple attempts for one Work item.

`you worker-sessions stream --provider <provider> --kind <kind> --id <id>` emits retained then live canonical events in order, terminates successfully after a terminal session, exits after replay for an already-terminal session, and propagates cancellation promptly with a stable interrupted result rather than hanging or leaking a subscription.

`you worker-sessions read --provider <provider> --kind <kind> --id <id>` renders the normalized transcript of a finished session and returns a clear non-success result when the session is missing, active, or its transcript is unavailable.

Every command has stable human output and `--output json` behavior: list/show/read emit deterministic JSON documents, stream emits one valid JSON object per NDJSON line, absent values are represented consistently, and machine-readable errors have stable codes while diagnostics go to stderr.

Focused command parsing/rendering and service/transport contract tests cover list, show, stream, and read for missing sessions, active streaming, finished transcripts, token usage, duration, and failure diagnostics; a `root.BuildProcess` functional scenario diagnoses recorded failed worker activity using only the new CLI and fails against the old missing-command behavior.

`go test ./tests/functional/provider_sessions/... -run TestWorkerSessionsCLI -count=1`, `make verify-fast`, typecheck, lint, and all affected tests pass; if a public API contract changes, authored OpenAPI sources and generated clients remain aligned via `make generate-api` and applicable API contract checks.

The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, every blocking PR conversation is explicitly addressed, shared-file or baseline conflicts are reconciled, merge conflicts are resolved, and the PR is actually merged; opened, green, approved, or ready-to-merge is not complete.

userStories.title: Expose an authoritative worker-session observation contract
userStories.description: As a CLI adapter maintainer, I want a provider-neutral observation contract over canonical session and recording projections so every command reports the same Work correlation, lifecycle, usage, duration, transcript availability, events, and failure facts.
acceptanceCriteria: A narrow service-root operation can query sessions by Work ID and query one session by its provider/kind/id identity without exposing recording internals, provider-reader implementations, filesystem handles, or storage paths.

Query results explicitly represent session identity, Work and attempt correlation, state, start/end timestamps, duration basis, token usage, transcript availability, and normalized failure/parse diagnostics; active duration is based on the injected clock and terminal duration is fixed by recorded timestamps.

A narrow cancellable stream operation replays retained canonical events in order and follows new events without polling raw provider storage; terminal completion, already-terminal replay, subscriber cancellation, and source failure are distinguishable outcomes.
Missing Work/session identities and unavailable projections return typed, safe, actionable errors suitable for stable CLI error mapping.
Focused service and projection contract tests cover multiple attempts, active and terminal sessions, token usage, duration, failure diagnostics, ordering, cancellation, and missing identities.
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Implemented the provider-neutral Worker Sessions observation contract, production Provider Sessions/Events wiring, deterministic Work correlation, lifecycle timing, normalized diagnostics, retained/live stream outcomes, and focused projection/stream/error tests. Review follow-up now injects the clock and Provider Sessions service directly through the canonical wire/runtime graph, with no optional constructor path, and keeps the root contract within the repository structure rules. Historical exact show and transcript reads now resolve identity and lifecycle from canonical Factory recording facts, then enrich normalized usage, parse, and transcript detail through Provider Sessions even when the process-local Worker Sessions registry is empty. The recorded-attempt regression test proves list to show to read to terminal replay with no live Worker Sessions service. Focused package tests, runtime/wire tests, race detection, make typecheck, the contracts check, and the UI suite pass.

userStories.title: List worker sessions for a Work item
userStories.description: As an operator, I want to list the sessions associated with a Work item so I can identify active, completed, retried, and failed attempts before choosing one to inspect.
acceptanceCriteria: `you worker-sessions list --work-id <id>` lists all authoritative correlated sessions in deterministic attempt/time order and shows provider, kind, session ID, Work ID, attempt, state, token totals, duration, and a concise failure indicator when present.

Human output uses a stable labeled/table presentation, represents unavailable token or timing values as `-`, and produces an explicit empty result rather than an ambiguous blank screen when the Work exists but has no sessions.
`--output json` emits one deterministic document with a `sessions` array; optional values are `null` rather than invented zero values, and stdout contains no progress or diagnostic prose.
A missing Work ID or unknown Work returns non-zero with a stable machine-readable error code in JSON mode and an actionable stderr message in human mode.
Focused parser, renderer, and transport contract tests prove populated, empty, missing, token-usage, duration, retry, and failed-session cases.
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Implemented the Work-correlated Worker Sessions REST and CLI list surfaces with deterministic chronological ordering, explicit known-empty and missing-Work behavior, stable human output, JSON nulls for unavailable optional values, token/duration/failure rendering, and generated contract/baseline synchronization. Review follow-up makes the runtime list projection authoritative from the canonical recording ledger/world-state projection, preserving historical attempts and explicit empty results while merging only normalized Provider Sessions detail. Replaced the five human-readable CLI documentation sourceHash placeholders with SHA-256 values from their owning production implementations and regenerated the package CLI contract and manifest through make contracts-generate. Added the measured 39.01% functional coverage floor for the new CLI transport package after CI identified its missing manifest entry. Focused Worker Sessions/HTTP/CLI/Wire tests, CLI manifest and contract smoke checks, make api-smoke, make verify-fast, backend-size, pkg-maint, package-file-count, and package-structure checks pass.

Invalid identity, missing session, unsupported provider/kind, and unavailable source return stable non-zero error behavior without leaking host storage paths or sensitive transcript content.

userStories.title: Stream retained and live session events
userStories.description: As an operator, I want to follow one worker session's canonical events so I can see current activity and its terminal outcome without polling logs.
acceptanceCriteria: `you worker-sessions stream --provider <provider> --kind <kind> --id <id>` emits retained events first and then live events exactly once in canonical order, including enough session/Work identity and event type information to correlate every line.
Human mode emits one stable, bounded line per event; `--output json` emits NDJSON with one complete object per line and no surrounding array, partial JSON, or non-JSON stdout text.

An active stream exits successfully after emitting its canonical terminal event; an already-terminal session replays through terminal and exits without waiting; a source failure returns non-zero after already-written complete records remain valid.

Ctrl-C or context cancellation is propagated to the subscription, stops further output promptly, releases resources, and exits with stable interrupted semantics (exit code 130 at the process boundary).

Focused parser, rendering, service/transport, and cancellation tests prove active-to-terminal, already-terminal, missing-session, source-failure, ordered replay/live handoff, JSON framing, and cancellation behavior without timing sleeps as the default synchronization mechanism.
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Implemented the retained-then-live Worker Session event stream over the canonical recording subscription, including explicit terminal, terminal-replay, source-failure, and cancellation outcomes. Added the session-scoped REST SSE endpoint, generated API/package/UI contract artifacts, and `you worker-sessions stream` with stable human lines, NDJSON framing, typed failures, and process-boundary cancellation exit code 130. Review follow-up now passes the effective stream limit and dispatch scope into the canonical ledger, bounds retained/live delivery without unrelated events consuming the buffer, and classifies terminal replay from the atomic retained snapshot; behavioral tests cover the active-to-terminal subscribe window and bounded history/live delivery. userStories.title: Read a finished session transcript

`--output json` emits one deterministic document containing session identity and an ordered `entries` array with structured entry fields; diagnostic prose never contaminates stdout.

Missing sessions, active/non-terminal sessions, unavailable transcripts, cancellation, and projection failures return distinct stable non-zero errors; the CLI never falls back to parsing raw rollout files.
Focused parser, renderer, and service/transport contract tests cover a finished transcript, tool activity, unavailable/encrypted content, active session, missing session, and failure diagnostics.
